bugs: Outcome counting is not idempotent. Under SQS at-least-once delivery a GenerateStatement that runs twice increments processed_accounts twice, so the run can finish and send the summary before every account has been attempted. A probe ran the same account twice in a 2-account run: it completed at processed=2 and sent the summary, while the second account was never attempted.

The summary mail is sent inline inside GenerateStatement (app/Jobs/GenerateStatement.php:70-72), after the run has already been claimed as finished. If that send throws, the job retries: it re-sends StatementReady to the account owner, increments processed_accounts again (so the count goes past the total), and finishIfAllAttempted returns false. The finance summary is never sent.
ShouldBeUnique/UniqueFor does nothing here because jobs are pushed with Queue::bulk, which skips PendingDispatch and so never takes the unique lock. The dedupe it appears to provide does not happen.

If an inactive account with id <= maxId is reactivated during fan-out, dispatched becomes larger than the initial total. processed_accounts can then reach the initial total before settleTotal runs, so the run finishes early with an incomplete count.
antipatterns: app/Jobs/GenerateStatement.php:25-27 ShouldBeUnique + #[UniqueFor] are ceremony that bulk dispatch never honours

app/Jobs/GenerateStatement.php:31-35 + app/Jobs/DispatchStatementChunk.php:43-46 the queue name is set three times (a QUEUE const, onQueue in the constructor, and the bulk queue: argument) instead of one #[Queue] attribute
app/Jobs/GenerateStatement.php:70-72 and app/Jobs/DispatchStatementChunk.php:56-58 the summary-mail logic is duplicated and sent inline instead of from its own job
app/Models/StatementRun.php:31-34 settleTotal mixes fresh() and forceFill/save on a stale instance
app/Models/StatementRun.php:36-43 two separate increments, not one atomic update
tests/Feature/StatementRunTest.php:22-28 runs the real queue:work with time travel, so the suite takes about 21s
strengths: The maxId bound plus settleTotal(dispatched_accounts) handles accounts deactivated during fan-out; a probe confirmed the run still completes and the summary is sent
Queue::bulk fan-out maps to SQS batch sends
The final status is claimed with a conditional UPDATE WHERE status=running, so only one worker sends the summary
Real retries with backoff for generator failures, and failed() counts the account once retries are used up; skips regenerating the PDF if it already exists
Markdown mailables with Blade views; #[Scope], #[Fillable] and queue attribute classes
End-to-end tests run a real worker, including the failure path and deactivation mid-run

bugs: total_accounts is counted in the action, but the dispatcher re-queries active accounts chunk by chunk later on. If an account is deactivated or deleted before its chunk is fanned out, processed_accounts never reaches total_accounts and the run stays 'running' forever with no summary. A probe confirmed this: total=2, processed=1, status running.

The reverse case: an account created or activated during fan-out gets a job too. The run completes when processed reaches the original total, so the summary goes out before every account has been attempted (probe: total=2, processed=3, completed).
Generator exceptions are caught and counted as final failures with no retry. Transient errors are never retried, even though the job declares #[Tries(3)].
antipatterns: app/Jobs/DispatchStatementJobs.php:43 dispatches 500 jobs one at a time instead of using Queue::bulk / SQS batch
app/Jobs/GenerateStatement.php:39-49 the catch-all Throwable around generation conflicts with the Tries/Backoff config
app/Models/StatementRun.php:39-41 uses increment with a DB::raw extra column; this works but a single update expression would read more clearly
app/Actions/StartStatementRun.php:16-17 passes counter defaults that the migration already sets
strengths: Cache::add dedupe in recordOutcome makes outcome counting idempotent across redelivery and the handle-then-failed path (probe confirmed), and the keys have a TTL so the cache does not grow
finishIfDone uses lockForUpdate in a transaction, and the summary is sent from a separate retryable SendStatementRunSummary job
#[Queue('statements'), Tries, Backoff, Timeout] attributes are idiomatic for Laravel 12/13; all slow work is off the default queue
Keyset-paginated self-chaining dispatcher with a composite (active,id) index; the request side does only a count and one dispatch
StatementReady attaches the PDF via Attachment::fromStorageDisk; a missing account is counted as failed
Fast, focused Pest tests cover failure counting, double delivery, failed(), a vanished account, the empty run and chunking

v.rationale:
I rank impl-2 first, but it's close. Both test suites pass (13 tests in impl-2, 11 in impl-1). I ran probes on each, and both have race bugs that break the rule that every run reaches a final status with an accurate failure count.

impl-2's bug is a drift between the account count and the accounts actually processed. It counts the active accounts at start, but the dispatcher picks accounts again later, chunk by chunk. If an account is deactivated before its chunk is sent out, the run stays 'running' forever (confirmed by probe). If one is added, the run finishes early.

impl-1 handles that drift correctly. It caps account ids at the start and then corrects the total to the number actually dispatched. But its outcome counting isn't protected against a job running twice: an SQS redelivery double-counts and finishes the run early (confirmed by probe). And because the summary email is sent inside the per-account job, a failed summary send triggers a retry that re-emails the customer, double-counts, and never delivers the summary. Its ShouldBeUnique setup looks like protection against this, but it does nothing because Queue::bulk skips the unique lock.

Beyond the bugs, impl-2 is cleaner and more idiomatic. It uses Cache::add to avoid double-counting (Redis is available), finishes the run under a row lock, sends the summary from its own retryable job, sets the queue with a single #[Queue] attribute, and attaches the PDF to the email. Its tests are fast and precise. impl-1 has more ceremony and repeats the summary logic in two places. Its main advantages are the Queue::bulk fan-out and genuine retries, and its end-to-end tests are realistic but slow (about 21s). So I weighed impl-1's correct handling of account changes against impl-2's protection from double-counting and better structure, and impl-2 comes out slightly ahead.
